data.title: WinVest Terminates Business Combination Agreement with Embed Financial
data.description:
WinVest Corp ( (WINV) ) has provided an update.

On November 9, 2026, Winvest Acquisition Corp. and Embed Financial Group Holdings, WinVest Merger Sub I Limited, WV Merger Sub II Corp. and Embed Financial Group Cayman Holdings mutually agreed to terminate their amended and restated business combination agreement, dated May 26, 2026, as amended. The contemplated transactions were abandoned, and the agreement became void except for provisions that expressly survived termination.

The termination automatically ended related ancillary documents other than confidentiality agreements and included mutual releases of claims and liabilities tied to the agreement, transaction documents, contemplated transactions and their termination. The parties agreed not to commence, encourage or assist in proceedings concerning released claims and to cooperate on termination steps, including withdrawing applicable governmental applications or proceedings; claims arising from a breach of the termination agreement were excluded from the releases.

data.title: KeyCorp Announces Redemption of Series E Preferred Shares
data.description:
KeyCorp ( (KEY) ) has shared an update.

On November 13, 2026, KeyCorp announced that it had given notice of its intention to redeem all 20,000,000 depositary shares representing its Series E Fixed-to-Floating Rate Perpetual Non-Cumulative Preferred Stock on December 15, 2026. The shares represented 500,000 preferred shares with a $500 million aggregate liquidation preference and were to be redeemed for $25.3828125 per depositary share, including accumulated and unpaid dividends through the redemption date.

Upon redemption, the preferred stock would no longer be outstanding, rights would terminate except for payment of the redemption price, and the stock would be delisted from the New York Stock Exchange. data.title: Aptera Reports Third-Quarter Losses Amid Going Concern Doubts
data.description:
Aptera Motors Corp. Class B ( (SEV) ) has provided an announcement.

On November 13, 2026, Aptera reported a third-quarter 2026 GAAP net loss of $14.0 million and a first-nine-month loss of $35.0 million; adjusted losses were $10.2 million and $23.5 million, respectively. As of September 30, the company had $9.2 million in cash and cash equivalents, including $4.1 million in refundable reservation fees, and had raised approximately $23.1 million in gross proceeds and $2.3 million in net proceeds during the first nine months.

In August 2026, Aptera ordered major parts for its initial production vehicles and entered a strategic partnership with Shanghai Launch Automotive Technology covering manufacturing and contract-engineering services of up to RMB 300 million. The company also announced certified service with RepairPal, while TÜV Rheinland measured more than 4 kilowatt-hours of usable solar energy delivered to the vehicle battery on each of three test days; Aptera said research and development spending more than doubled as resources shifted toward vehicle validation and production readiness. The company said its existing cash was not sufficient to fund operations for the next 12 months and that substantial doubt about its ability to continue as a going concern had not been alleviated.

data.title: SDR Drone Enters Agreement for Proposed Financing Placement
data.description:
An announcement from SDR Drone ( (SDCO) ) is now available.

On November 10, 2026, SDR Drone, Inc., a Florida corporation, entered an engagement with Dawson James Securities to serve as lead placement agent, on a best-efforts, non-exclusive basis, for a proposed bridge financing and/or private placement of convertible debt, equity or equity-linked securities. The engagement targeted gross proceeds of $2.5 million to $3 million, while Dawson James had no obligation to buy securities or ensure a successful placement.

Terms included a non-refundable $50,000 retainer credited against a 7% fee on proceeds from investors introduced by Dawson James, plus five-year warrants equal to 3% of securities issued to those investors, exercisable at 110% of the offering price. Because the company was subject to a Rule 506(d) disqualifying order, the offering was to rely on Section 4(a)(2), with restrictions including no general solicitation and sales only to accredited investors; no retainer note had been issued or purchaser identified at the time.

data.title: PVAC Proxy Seeks Vote on Proposed Tigerless Health Combination
data.description:
New activity is brewing for Capitalworks Emerging Markets Acquisition Corp Class A ( (CMCAF) ). The company has submitted a Form DEFM14A to the SEC, indicating an upcoming shareholder vote. This form gives shareholders all the information they need to develop an informed vote. Read on to learn more about the proposed company action.

Piermont Valley Acquisition Corp. filed a definitive proxy for a Dec. 9, 2026, virtual extraordinary meeting to vote on its proposed combination with Tigerless Health, Inc. At closing, PVAC ordinary shares would convert into Pubco Class A shares, while outstanding PVAC warrants would become Pubco warrants on substantially similar terms. data.title: CSN Reports R$1,247.3 Million Net Loss in 3Q26
data.description:
An update from Companhia Siderúrgica Nacional ( (SID) ) is now available.

Companhia Siderúrgica Nacional operates steel, mining, cement and energy businesses, including iron ore mining and steel operations. On November 12, 2026, it reported third-quarter net revenue of R$10,485.8 million, down 7.3% from 2Q26 and 11.1% from 3Q25. Adjusted EBITDA fell 32.3% sequentially and 43.5% year over year to R$1,875.9 million, while its margin declined 6.4 and 9.8 percentage points, respectively.

CSN said lower iron ore prices and higher seaborne freight costs weighed on mining, while seasonal weakness affected European steel operations. Steel benefited from operational and pricing improvements, and cement delivered record performance, but the mining segment remained the main source of pressure on profitability.

The company reported a net loss of R$1,247.3 million, compared with net income in 3Q25, as weaker operating performance and other operating expenses affected results. Free cash flow was negative by R$3.5 billion in 3Q26, reversing the positive result of the previous quarter because of weaker operating results and significant debt amortization.

data.title: Mako Mining Reports Q3 2026 Results With $30.3 Million Adjusted EBITDA
data.description:
The latest update is out from Mako Mining Corp ( (TSE:MKO) ).

Mako Mining is a publicly listed gold mining, development and exploration company that operates the San Albino gold mine in Nicaragua and the Moss Mine in Arizona. It also owns the permitted Mt. Hamilton heap-leach project in Nevada and holds the PEA-stage Eagle Mountain Project in Guyana.

For the three months ended September 30, 2026, Mako reported revenue of $50.7 million, Adjusted EBITDA of $30.3 million, Mine OCF of $22.4 million and net income of $16.4 million, or $0.19 per share. It sold 11,581 ounces of gold at an average realized price of $4,292 per ounce and reported $2,890 AISC per ounce sold, $119.3 million in cash, trade receivables and marketable securities, and $4.0 million in exploration and evaluation expenses.
